qa_triage.pins_are_snapshot_of: Snapshot D: an independent exact-SHA LOCAL rerun at the real daemon boundary, with a red->green control. The same probe exits 1 on fdc223f (10 failures) and 0 on 7a87e5c with 33/33 checks. QA_PARTIAL with no signature and no PASS.

findings.summary: intent_digest omitted session_ref and agent_runtime, so the same key sent to another session or runtime was answered as a REPLAY. Snapshot C closes this at LOCAL: target, runtime and principal are in the digest, all three axes return CONFLICT, and no/expired context and self-asserted principal are refused.

The observation-to-SETTLED judgment was not wired into the production path and the write entry could self-attest. Snapshot D closes the effect-safety half at LOCAL with a red->green control: D3, D4 and D10 are closed and regressions D1/D2/D5-D9/D11-D14 hold. The residual is P1: owner-observation reconcile still has no production caller.

D3 cross-actor forgery: another trusted actor could settle A's attempt using A's copied digest and a fabricated result. Snapshot D closes this at LOCAL: the write is refused UNTRUSTED_ACTOR and the attempt is unchanged.

D4 terminal-state regression: a terminal SETTLED could be written back to CALL_NOT_SENT, after which the kernel returns PROCEED, so a retry becomes a second effect. Snapshot D closes this at LOCAL: an authentic SETTLED cannot move to CALL_NOT_SENT or EFFECT_UNKNOWN, EFFECT_UNKNOWN cannot move back, and a terminal retry is REPLAY.

test_no_node_paths_in_product_data.py failed at 494f452 on an inherited absolute home literal in fleet_mcp/deploy/release_plan.py. Snapshot B re-ran the full guard independently at 4a5d0a0: 10 tests OK, exit 0 (LOCAL). Closed at that SHA.

G1 present-but-null is read as an affirmative answer: {"health": null, "policy": null} yields READY/ALLOWED and a non-null effective, so a negative invariant is bypassed. The QA artifact rates this P1; the campaign brief called it P0 — recorded here at the rate the evidence supports.

_same_writer matched an empty or partial writer record; an empty current_writer equalled a reconciler with every field absent. Snapshot D closes this at LOCAL (D10): empty writer, no-principal record and empty reconciler all refuse.
Owner-observation reconcile still has no production caller: the kernel is correct but nothing invokes it on the real path. Grant enforcement was not exercised in this probe (SOURCE/NOT_RUN).
I1 manifest drift: earlier manifests pinned stale heads and omitted new candidates. Fixed in manifest -e, which pins fdc223f, 4a5d0a0, 619cf63, c2e2e8d and QA Snapshot C a9c3ea5.

Gate level inconsistency: FLEET_NEXT_33_6 requires REAL_DEVICE while its supporting rows are SOURCE. This is intentional — a gate may require more than it has and then reports BLOCKED — but it must not be read as a near-PASS.

drift_guard.policy: Every pin is re-read from the provider API immediately before push and again before composition. A candidate whose observed_at precedes snapshot_time is stale and must be re-pinned, never assumed. An independent QA triage signs a snapshot, not a branch name.

conflict_audit.conclusion: Siblings from merge-base 008a3360 (#200 head). Their own-commit surfaces are 22 and 13 files with an empty intersection; 163 files shared in the net sets are inherited ancestry, not collision. #243 has since advanced by one guard commit.
The safety line is file-disjoint from the Fleet, G1 and Core lanes. Semantic coupling remains: #241 edits fleet/agent-control-contract.yaml while F1 adds fleet/fleet-mcp-contract.yaml.

Same repository, disjoint directories: the seams write only integrations/fleet-v1-{runtime-parity,verdict-evidence,network-health}/** plus one test each, and no lane candidate writes those paths.
